Friedrich Air Conditioning Recalls KÜHL Window Air Conditioners Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Fire and Burn Hazards

  • Share:

  • Share it on Facebook
  • Share it on Twitter
  • Copy Link
  • Print Page
  • Copy link
  • Recalled KÜHL® Q Air Conditioner
  • The model and serial number are location inside the Kühl® Q Air Conditioner
  • A close up of serial and model number are location inside the Kühl® Q Air Conditioner
  • Recalled KÜHL® S Air Conditioner
  • The model and serial number are location inside the Kühl® S Air Conditioner
  • Close-up of the model and serial number are location inside the Kühl® S Air Conditioner
Name of Product:
Kühl® Q and Kühl® S Window Air Conditioners 
Hazard:

The control board inside the motor of the recalled air conditioners can fail, posing a risk of serious injury or death from fire and burn hazards.

Remedy:
Refund
Replace
Recall Date:
September 17, 2026
Units:

About 2,000

Consumer Contact

Friedrich Air Conditioning toll-free at 800-541-6645 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT, Monday through Friday, or online at www.friedrich.com/product-recall  or online at www.friedrich.com and click on “Recall Information” at the bottom of the page. 

WebsitePhone

Recall Details

Description:

This recall involves KÜHL Q and KÜHL S Window Air Conditioners. The products have a gray front and a black air discharge grille and have the name Friedrich and the Friedrich logo in the lower left corner of the unit. The Kühl Q front control panel is located on the top left corner of the unit, and the Kühl S front control panel is located on the right side of the unit below the discharge grille. The models are KCVQ08B10A, KHVQ10B11A, KCVS08B10A, KCVS12B10A, KCVS12B30A and KCVS16B30A. The model and serial number are located inside the air conditioners. Only some serial numbers below have motors that are included in this recall.   

Remedy:

Consumers should stop using the recalled air conditioners immediately and visit www.friedrich.com/product-recall to receive information on how to determine if their unit is covered by the recall. Consumers should have the air conditioner’s serial number, which can be found on the inside of the unit, when they visit the recall web page or call Friedrich about the recall. If your unit has a serial number that is included in the recall, the firm will send you instructions on how to obtain a refund or free replacement unit. 

Incidents/Injuries:

The firm has received two reports indicating that the air conditioner’s motor ignited, with one incident causing smoke and fire damage to a residence. No injuries have been reported. 

Sold At:
PC Richard & Son, Grainger, and Johnson Supply stores and other appliance distributors and retailers nationwide from January 2026 through August 2026 for between $1,300 and $2,000.
Importer(s):

Friedrich Air Conditioning Co., of San Antonio, Texas 

Manufactured In:
Mexico
Recall number:
26-776
Fast Track Recall

Related Recalls

Char-Broil Recalls Bistro Pro Electric Grills Due to Risk of Electric Shock

The grounding wire for the grill’s heating element can disconnect and lose fault protection, posing an electric shock hazard.  

Clorox Puerto Rico Recalls 6 Million Scented Mistolin and Lestoil Multi-Purpose Cleaners Due to Risk of Exposure to Bacteria

The recalled products may contain bacteria, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which is an environmental organism found widely in soil and water. People with weakened immune systems or external medical devices who are exposed to Pseudomonas aeruginosa face a risk of serious infection that may require medical treatment. The bacteria can enter the body if inhaled, through the eyes, or through a break in the skin. People with healthy immune systems are usually not affected by the bacteria.

Daikin Comfort Technologies Manufacturing Recalls Amana Through-The-Wall Air Conditioners and Heat Pumps Due to Risk of Serious Injury from Fire

The snubber circuit can emit flames if it shorts, posing a risk of serious injury due to fire hazard. 

Rowenta Recalls Cordless Vacuum Cleaners Due to Risk of Serious Injury from Fire and Burn Hazards

The recalled lithium-ion battery in the vacuum cleaner can overheat and ignite, posing a risk of serious injury from fire and burn hazards.

About the U.S. CPSC

The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) is charged with protecting the public from unreasonable risk of injury associated with the use of thousands of types of consumer products. Deaths, injuries, and property damage from consumer product-related incidents cost the nation more than $1 trillion annually. Since the CPSC was established more than 50 years ago, it has worked to ensure the safety of consumer products, which has contributed to a decline in injuries associated with these products.

Federal law prohibits any person from selling products subject to a Commission ordered recall or a voluntary recall undertaken in consultation with the CPSC.
